NDT training in Saskatoon, SK: a practical guide for technicians and employers

Short answer: Saskatoon technicians can complete NDT theory online, mostly self-paced and with ASNT NDT Level III support, then take the hands-on practical at their employer's site. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Saskatoon. Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and fit employers whose customers specify ASNT. They do not replace CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification, which is issued by NRCan or CWB Group. We reply within one business day.

Saskatoon's industrial economy is built on what comes out of the ground. Potash mines and processing sites ring the city, uranium producers run their head offices here and operate mines and mills far to the north, and a large agricultural machinery and manufacturing sector keeps welding shops busy year-round. All of that creates demand for people who can find a crack, measure a wall or interpret a weld image, and for employers who need those people qualified on paper.

The first decision for anyone training here is which scheme the work requires. Mining and uranium employers in Saskatchewan sit in a regulated environment where the licence, the client or the quality programme decides how NDT personnel must be certified. Some specify the Canadian national standard, CAN/CGSB-48.9712. Others, especially suppliers building equipment for US customers or working to ASME and AWS codes, specify ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Our courses are for the second group. Atlantis NDT is not a Recognized Training Organization for NRCan or CWB Group, so anyone aiming at a CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certificate should take method training from one of those organisations.

If SNT-TC-1A fits your work, tell us what you need in Saskatoon: methods, levels and how many people.

How to get NDT certified in Saskatoon under SNT-TC-1A

  1. Identify the governing document. Look at the contract, the client's quality specification and the code edition. Note whether it names a scheme and which edition.
  2. Put the written practice on paper. The employer's written practice is the rulebook for hours, experience, examinations and renewal. Companies new to SNT-TC-1A can have one drafted through written practice development.
  3. Study the theory online. Each method has a course for each level, studied on the Atlantis portal on your own timetable. Compare the hours against your written practice using the training-requirements matrix.
  4. Build documented experience. Time in the method counts when a supervisor signs for it. Keep a log from the first day.
  5. Pass the written papers. A general examination on method principles and a specific one on your employer's equipment, procedures and codes.
  6. Demonstrate the practical. Examine real specimens at the employer's facility while a Level III watches and grades the result.
  7. Clear the vision check. Near vision and colour discrimination are tested and recorded.
  8. Be certified by the employer. The company issues the certificate under its written practice.
  9. Plan renewal. Renewal follows the practice. If you also hold a national certificate, keep both calendars.

People who prefer a credential that stays with them can aim for ASNT central certification, which ASNT examines and issues. Check your hours and eyesight against the published criteria using the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker before you enrol.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Saskatoon technicians

The courses below follow the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge. The last column shows how each method links to the kind of work found around Saskatoon, which is how practical exercises are chosen.

MethodCourse contentWhere Saskatoon work uses it
UTSound physics, calibration, thickness measurement, weld examination, reading A-scan and B-scan displaysCorrosion surveys on tanks and vessels at mining and processing sites, weld checks on fabricated equipment
PAUT and TOFDBeam steering, focal laws, encoded scanning, sizing from diffracted signalsHeavy-section welds on vessels and structures, weld checks where code permits advanced UT
RTRadiation sources, exposure geometry, density and sensitivity, image interpretationPressure-vessel and piping welds, castings, shop fabrication
MTMagnetisation, particle selection, yokes and coils, demagnetisationWelds on trailers, implements and structural steel, heavy mobile equipment repair
PTPenetrant types, cleaning, dwell, developer, evaluationStainless and aluminium parts, food and fertiliser-handling equipment
VTVisual acuity, illumination, measuring tools, discontinuity recognitionEvery fabrication shop; first-line inspection on structures and vessels
ETImpedance-plane analysis, probe frequency, tube testingHeat-exchanger tubes, surface checks on non-ferrous parts

Level I is the starting point, Level II is the working qualification for most employers, and Level III is the technical authority who writes procedures and examines others. Learn more at Level 1 training, Level 2 training and the Level III programme.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Saskatoon

Ultrasonic testing is a strong first method in Saskatoon because the mining and processing economy is full of steel that corrodes. Tanks hold brines and process liquors, vessels carry chemicals, and structural steel lives outdoors through hard winters. A technician who can gauge thickness reliably and read weld indications is useful from the first week.

The UT course explains how an ultrasonic beam travels, reflects and weakens, how to set up and check an instrument before use, and why a reading means nothing unless the calibration is right. It also covers the practical traps: scale and pitting that scatter sound, curved surfaces, coatings, and the effect of cold on couplant and equipment. Saskatoon's winters make that last point more than theoretical. Instruments that behave in a heated shop can behave differently at minus twenty on a tank wall.

Further detail is on the UT training page. For a second method, many technicians add MT or PT, because surface-breaking cracks are a common finding in welded equipment and those methods are quick to learn once UT is established.

Where NDT technicians work around Saskatoon

Potash and mineral processing. Mines and mills around the city depend on large vessels, conveyors, pipe networks and storage structures. Inspection contractors and in-house reliability teams examine them for corrosion and fatigue, and new mine construction brings weld examination on steel and pressure equipment.

Uranium. Several major uranium producers are headquartered in Saskatoon and run operations in the north of the province. Those licensed sites answer to the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission and run their own qualification programmes. Contractors and suppliers to that industry may be asked for particular schemes, so always confirm with the customer before choosing a course. Our SNT-TC-1A training is relevant to supply-chain work that specifies it and is not a route into in-service inspection where the licensee names another scheme.

Manufacturing and agricultural equipment. Seeders, grain handling equipment, trailers and tanks are made in and around the city. Welds on these products are examined by visual, magnetic particle and penetrant methods, with ultrasonic or radiographic work where the product or customer calls for it.

Pipelines and oilfield service. Saskatchewan has an active oil and gas sector, with pipelines to CSA Z662 and provincial or federal oversight depending on the route. Saskatoon-based contractors support that work with weld examination and integrity checks.

Pressure equipment. Boilers and pressure vessels in the province fall under the Technical Safety Authority of Saskatchewan. Check current requirements directly with the authority.

Research and public sector. A university, a research council and agricultural research facilities create occasional demand for specialist non-destructive evaluation, mostly on materials and equipment rather than field welds.

NDT schools and classes near Saskatoon: what to compare

Anyone looking for NDT classes near Saskatoon should compare formats, not just names. A polytechnic or college programme is the best fit for someone entering the trade without a job lined up, because it offers a long, broad introduction. A contractor's in-house course is fast and relevant but tied to that company. An online theory course with a practical at the employer suits people already working, or hired on condition that they qualify.

Put these questions to every provider:

  • Does the course lead into the scheme my employer or customer names?
  • Who issues the final certificate?
  • Are practical examinations performed on real specimens, and who grades them?
  • Does the syllabus match published hour recommendations or a written practice?
  • Can the training records be used if I move jobs?

Be careful with any provider that says a course certifies you. Under SNT-TC-1A only the employer certifies. The NDT training FAQ covers many of these points, and the training overview lists every method and level.

Online NDT training in Saskatchewan

The online theory course runs on the Atlantis portal. It is mainly self-paced, an ASNT NDT Level III is available for questions, and access begins as soon as you enrol. Because courses run all year, there is no waiting for a start. Technicians who rotate to remote northern sites can download material in advance and study offline when connectivity is poor.

The online format covers theory only. The practical, which is where skill is demonstrated, happens at the employer with real specimens. See online NDT training and the Saskatchewan training overview for more.

Training a crew at your Saskatoon facility

Employers who need a group of technicians qualified together can organise the programme around their own premises. Each person studies theory online. The practical block takes place at your shop, plant or yard with your equipment and representative specimens, and a Level III administers the examinations and reviews the records.

Common triggers include a fabricator winning work for a US customer, a service company adding methods to its scope, and a processing site renewing a team as experienced staff retire. Use the crew training enquiry to describe your situation, or ask about outsourced Level III support if you lack an in-house Level III. For Canada, contact us for fees in your region.

ASNT SNT-TC-1A suits employers whose customers specify ASNT, such as shops shipping to US projects, firms on cross-border work and suppliers into nuclear and aerospace supply chains. It does not satisfy requirements that name CAN/CGSB-48.9712.

Radiography licensing in Saskatchewan

Radiography in Canada is governed federally. The Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission licenses the organisations that hold exposure devices, and operators must be CNSC-certified exposure device operators or work directly under one. Provincial occupational health and safety legislation adds its own radiation requirements.

A radiographic testing course teaches how to produce and interpret images. It does not authorise anyone to handle a source. Atlantis NDT does not provide exposure device operator training, so arrange that separately with your employer.

Practise before your practical exam

Rehearse on the Practical NDT simulator, which runs in a browser and lets you work through set-ups and indications in simulated workplaces. It supports repetition between sessions, but it never stands in for the practical on real specimens. Test your written knowledge with the NDT practice tests.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Saskatoon

How do I start an NDT career in Saskatoon?

Begin with a Level I course in a method your target employers use, such as UT or VT, and look for trainee roles in fabrication, mining service or inspection. Your employer then certifies you under its written practice as you gain experience.

Is there an NDT school in Saskatoon?

Atlantis NDT does not operate a school there. Our model is online theory plus a practical at your employer. For a campus programme, look at the provincial college and polytechnic options and check which certification scheme they feed.

Can I do NDT training online in Saskatchewan?

Theory, yes. The practical examination needs real specimens and happens in person at the employer.

Does your course give me CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification?

No. That certificate comes from NRCan or CWB Group after training from a Recognized Training Organization, and Atlantis NDT is not one. Our courses prepare you for SNT-TC-1A or ASNT central certification.

Which method should I learn first?

Match the method to the local work. UT suits corrosion surveys at mining and processing sites, and VT, MT and PT suit fabrication.

What jobs use NDT in Saskatoon?

Mining and mineral processing, uranium supply chains, agricultural equipment manufacturing, pipeline and oilfield service, and fabrication all employ technicians.

Do I need a licence for radiography?

Yes, to operate an exposure device you need CNSC exposure device operator certification. An NDT course certificate does not replace it.

What happens to my certificate if I change employers?

An SNT-TC-1A certificate belongs to the employer that issued it, so the next employer recertifies you. An ASNT central certificate belongs to you.

How much does training cost?

For Canada, contact us for fees in your region. We reply within one business day, and Register and Buy Now opens the course on the Atlantis portal.

Who teaches the courses?

Anoop Rayavarapu leads the training. He is an ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT with more than eleven years of international field experience.
